ex.ja: トムはゴム手袋をはめた。

en: Having to do with or arranged in a series.
Who performs a specified action or course of action repeatedly or regularly.
A literary or dramatic work, such as a radio or television programme, published in installments, often numbered and without a specified end.
A publication issued in successive parts, often numbered and with no predetermined end.
to assign a serial number to (especially of aircraft)

serial.ety: Formed as series + -al, on model of Latin seriālis, from seriēs + -ālis. Cognate to Italian seriale. First use appears c. 1823. See cite below.

ex.en: The police suspect Tom is a serial killer.
ex.ja: 警察は、トムが連続殺人犯だとにらんでいる。

ex.en: The television serial is getting more and more interesting.
ex.ja: その番組はだんだんおもしろくなってきた。

ex.en: Last year's pop hit was set off by a serial TV drama.
ex.ja: 去年のヒットした音楽は、みんな人気ドラマが絡んでいる。

note.ja: series（連続）+ -al。ラテン語 serere（つなぐ）。「連続の」。series と同じ。

en: To part with, separate from, leave off; cast off, cast, let fall, be divested of.
To allow to flow or fall.
An opening between upper and lower warp yarns through which the weft is woven.
An area of land as distinguished from those around it.

shed.ety:
From Middle English scheden, schede, from Old English scēadan, scādan (“to separate, divide, part, make a line of separation between; remove from association or companionship; distinguish, discriminate, decide, determine, appoint; shatter, shed; expound; decree; write down; differ”), from Proto-West Germanic *skaiþan, from Proto-Germanic *skaiþaną (compare West Frisian skiede, Dutch and German scheiden), from Proto-Indo-European *skeyt- (“to cut, part, divide, separate”), from *skey-.
See also Irish scian (“knife”), Lithuanian skėsti (“to spread”), ski̇́esti (“to separate”), Old Church Slavoni

ex.en: I cannot read this book without shedding tears.
ex.ja: 私はこの本を読むと必ず涙を流します。

ex.en: Such was her joy that she shed tears.
ex.ja: 彼女の喜びは非常なものだったので、彼女は涙を流したのです。

ex.en: She shed tears while listening to the story.
ex.ja: 彼女はその話を聞いて涙を流した。

note.ja: 「流す・落とす」は古英語 scēadan（分ける）から。「小屋」は shade（陰）の変化とされ別語。

en: Any of the suborder Serpentes of legless reptiles with long, thin bodies and fork-shaped tongues.
A person who acts deceitfully for personal or social gain; a treacherous person.
To follow or move in a winding route.
To clean using a plumbing snake.

ex.en: I'm not in the least afraid of snakes.
ex.ja: 私は蛇など全然怖くない。

ex.en: She drew back when she saw a snake.
ex.ja: 彼女は蛇を見て退いた。

ex.en: It's not good to wake a sleeping snake.
ex.ja: 藪をつついてヘビを出す。

note.ja: 古英語 snaca から。sneak（こっそり動く）と同系。

en: A person or organization with some sort of responsibility for another person or organization, especially where the responsibility has a r…
A senior member of a twelve step or similar program chosen to guide an initiate and form a partnership with them.
To be a sponsor for.

sponsor.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin spōnsor (“a surety", in Late Latin "a sponsor in baptism”).

ex.en: This program has the following sponsors.
ex.ja: この番組はご覧のスポンサーの提供でお送りします。

ex.en: All the expenses will fall on the sponsor.
ex.ja: その費用はみな発起人にかかります。

ex.en: This program has been brought to you by the following sponsors.
ex.ja: この番組はご覧のスポンサーの提供でお送りします。

note.ja: spons（約束する）+ or（人）。保証を約束する人 →「保証人・後援者・スポンサー」。

en: Strained; drawn close; tight.
Tense; not relaxed.

strict.ety: Borrowed from Latin strictus, past participle of stringere (“to draw tight, bind, contract”). Doublet of strait and stretto. See stringent, strain. Related to strong.

ex.en: Our English teacher is both strict and kind.
ex.ja: 私たちの英語の先生は、厳格であるがまた親切でもある。

ex.en: My mother is strict, but my father isn't.
ex.ja: 私のお母さんは厳しいけど、お父さんはそんなことないよ。

ex.en: Neither of my parents is strict with me.
ex.ja: 両親がふたりとも私に厳しいわけではない。

note.ja: ラテン語 strictus（締めつけられた）から。きつく締めた →「厳しい・厳密な」。restrict（制限する）、district（地区）も同じ。

en: Following, afterwards in either time or place.
Accordingly, therefore (implying a logical connection or deduction), consequently.

subsequently.ety:
Etymology tree
English subsequent
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English subsequently
From subsequent + -ly.

ex.en: He caught a cold and subsequently missed the exam.
ex.ja: 彼は風邪をひき、その後試験を受けられなかった。

note.ja: subsequent（その後の）+ -ly。「その後」。

en: Physical matter; material.
A form of matter that has constant chemical composition and characteristic properties.

substance.ety: Inherited from Middle English substance, from Old French substance, from Latin substantia (“substance, essence”), from substāns, present active participle of substō (“exist”, literally “stand under”), from sub + stō (“stand”). Displaced native Old English andweorc.

ex.en: It was an argument of little substance.
ex.ja: ほとんど内容のない議論だった。

ex.en: The substance must be treated with acid.
ex.ja: その物質は酸で処理しなければならない。

ex.en: Tell me the substance of his speech.
ex.ja: 彼のスピーチの主旨を教えてください。

note.ja: sub（下に）+ stan（立つ）+ ce。下に立って支えるもの →「物質・実質・本質」。

en: A neutral party in a dispute; one who does not take sides.

Switzerland.ety: Compound of Switzer + -land, adopted in the 16th century from Early Modern German Schwytzerland (“land of the Swiss”). Noun sense refers to the state’s political neutrality in both World Wars.

ex.en: My mom wants me to study in Switzerland.
ex.ja: 母は私をスイスに留学させたがっている。

ex.en: My mother wants me to study in Switzerland.
ex.ja: 母は私をスイスに留学させたがっている。

ex.en: Switzerland is a beautiful country worth visiting.
ex.ja: スイスは訪れる価値のある美しい国です。

note.ja: Swiss + land。シュヴィーツ（Schwyz）州の名前から。

en: A recognizable pattern of signs, symptoms and/or behaviours, especially of a disease or medical or psychological condition.
Any set of characteristics regarded as identifying a certain type, condition, etc., usually adverse.

syndrome.ety: Learned borrowing from New Latin syndrome, from Ancient Greek συνδρομή (sundromḗ, “concurrence of symptoms, concourse”), from σύνδρομος (súndromos, “running together”), from συν- (sun-, “with”) + δρόμος (drómos, “running, course”).

ex.en: Jet lag is a syndrome many travelers suffer from.
ex.ja: 時差ぼけは多くの旅行者が悩まされる症候群だ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 syndromē（共に走ること）から。syn + dramein（走る）。「同時に起こる症状の集まり」→「症候群」。

ex.ja: 注意深かったのに彼は思いがけない間違いをした。

ex.en: For Tom, getting fired was an unexpected shock.
ex.ja: トムにとって、解雇は予想外のショックだった。

ex.en: Save money against the unexpected for when it's necessary.
ex.ja: いざというときのために貯金する。

note.ja: un（否定）+ expected（予期された）。「予想外の」。

Custom, tradition.

ex.ja: これは現代英語の慣用法についての本です。

ex.en: He has an eye for good English usage.
ex.ja: 彼は正しい英語の使い方を良く知っている。

ex.en: This car must have had tough usage.
ex.ja: この車は乱暴な使い方をされてきたに違いない。

note.ja: use（使う）+ -age。「使用法・語法」。

Unintentionally.

ex.en: I accidentally forgot to bring the house key.
ex.ja: 家の鍵、持ってくるの忘れちゃった。

ex.en: They say that true happiness is found accidentally.
ex.ja: 純粋な幸せは偶然に見つかるって言ってた。

note.ja: accidental（偶然の）+ -ly。ad + cadere（落ちる）。「降りかかって」→「偶然に・誤って」。accident と同じ cad。

en: A person attached to a particular pursuit, study, science, or art (such as music or painting), especially one who cultivates any study, i…
Someone who is unqualified or insufficiently skillful.
Non-professional.
Created, done, or populated by amateurs or non-professionals.

amateur.ety: Borrowed from French amateur, from Latin amātor (“lover”), from amāre (“to love”).

ex.en: You are a professional, but I am an amateur.
ex.ja: あなたはプロだが私はアマチュアだ。

ex.en: My uncle is an amateur cricket player.
ex.ja: 私のおじはアマチュアのクリケット選手です。

ex.en: You're a professional, and I'm an amateur.
ex.ja: あなたはプロで、私はアマチュア。

note.ja: フランス語 amateur（愛好家）から。ラテン語 amator（愛する人）、amare（愛する）。「好きでする人」。amour と同じ。

The living organisms of a particular region.

ex.ja: 彼は生物学の分野で研究している。

ex.ja: 生物のテストどうだった？

ex.en: He is very much interested in biology.
ex.ja: 彼は生物学に非常に関心をもっている。

en: In a brief manner, summarily.
For a brief period.

briefly.ety: From Middle English breefly, breffly, brevely, brevelike, breveliche, equivalent to brief + -ly.

ex.en: To put it briefly, I do not agree.
ex.ja: 簡単に言えば、私は賛成しません。

ex.en: I explained briefly to him how it happened.
ex.ja: 僕は彼に事件のいきさつを一通り話した。

ex.en: The speaker treated the subject very briefly.
ex.ja: 講演者はその問題をきわめて簡潔に論じた。

note.ja: brief（短い）+ -ly。「簡潔に・少しの間」。

en: An artificial waterway or artificially improved river used for travel, shipping, or irrigation.
A tubular channel within the body or within a plant.
To dig an artificial waterway in or to (a place), especially for drainage
To travel along a canal by boat

canal.ety: Borrowed from Middle French canal, from Old French canal, from Latin canālis (“channel, canal, narrow passage”), from canna (“reed, cane”), from Ancient Greek κάννα (kánna, “reed”), from Akkadian 𒄀 (qanû, “reed”). Doublet of channel. See also cane and -al.

ex.en: This ship is too big to pass through the canal.
ex.ja: この船は大きすぎて運河を通れない。

ex.en: The canal connects the Atlantic with the Pacific.
ex.ja: その運河は大西洋と太平洋をつないでいる。

ex.en: Canals have been built to irrigate the desert.
ex.ja: 砂漠に水を引くために運河が建設されている。

note.ja: ラテン語 canalis（水路・管）から。「運河」。channel と同じ語源。

en: To cross out something with lines etc.
To invalidate or annul something.
A cancellation.
A control message posted to Usenet that serves to cancel a previously posted message.

cancel.ety: From Middle English cancellen, from Anglo-Norman canceler (“to cross out with lines”) (modern French chanceler (“to stagger, sway”)), from Old French canceler, from Latin cancellō (“to make resemble a lattice”), from cancellus (“a railing or lattice”), diminutive of cancer (“a lattice”).

ex.en: Otherwise we will have to cancel this order.
ex.ja: もし無理な場合は注文をキャンセルします。

ex.en: If you have any sense, cancel the trip.
ex.ja: 多少でも分別があるなら旅行は中止するんだな。

ex.en: We have to cancel our trip to Japan.
ex.ja: 日本旅行は中止しなければいけない。

note.ja: ラテン語 cancellare（格子状に線を引く）から。cancelli（格子）。文書に×の線を引いて「取り消す」。

en: To traverse a slope or contour, either upwards (ascending) or downwards (descending).
(literally or figuratively): To ascend; rise; to go up.
An act of climbing.
The act of getting to somewhere more elevated.

climb.ety: From Middle English climben, clymben, from Old English climban (“to climb”), from Proto-West Germanic *klimban, from Proto-Germanic *klimbaną (“to climb, go up by clinging”), believed to be a nasalised variant of Proto-Germanic *klibaną, *klibāną (“to stick, cleave”), from Proto-Indo-European *gley- (“to stick”). Cognate with West Frisian klimme (“to climb”), Dutch klimmen (“to climb”), German klimmen (“to climb”), Old Norse klembra (“to squeeze”), Icelandic klifra (“to climb”). Related to clamber. See also clay, glue.

ex.en: We climbed along the stream in the mountains.
ex.ja: 我々は山の中で小川に沿って登った。

ex.en: With great effort he climbed up the tree.
ex.ja: 一所懸命になって彼はその木に登った。

ex.en: It's not absolutely impossible to climb the mountain.
ex.ja: その山に登るのは全く不可能というわけではない。

note.ja: 古英語 climban から。「登る」。b は発音しない。

The conclusion of an act of conveyancing concerning the sale of a property.

ex.ja: この建物は完成間近だ。

en: A sea or lake voyage, especially one taken for pleasure.
Portion of aircraft travel at a constant airspeed and altitude between ascent and descent phases.
To sail about, especially for pleasure.
To travel at constant speed for maximum operating efficiency.

cruise.ety: Borrowed from Dutch kruisen (“cross, sail around”), from kruis (“cross”), from Middle Dutch cruce, from Latin crux.

ex.en: How many cruises are there each day?
ex.ja: １日に何便有りますか。

ex.en: He cruised his way through the crowd.
ex.ja: 彼は群集を押し分けて進んだ。

ex.en: We are cruising at an altitude of 39,000 feet.
ex.ja: 我々は、39,000フィートの上空を航行中です。

note.ja: オランダ語 kruisen（交差する）から。kruis（十字）。行ったり来たりして「巡航する」。cross と同じ語源。

en: The legal right to take care of something or somebody, especially children.
Temporary possession or care of somebody else's property.

custody.ety: Borrowed from Latin custōdia (“a keeping, watch, guard, prison”), from custōs (“a keeper, watchman, guard”). Doublet of custode.

ex.en: Her husband also wanted custody of the children.
ex.ja: 旦那も子供の引き取り権を望んでいた。

ex.en: But custody of the children was a problem.
ex.ja: 問題は子供の引き取り権だった。

ex.en: The man was held in police custody.
ex.ja: その男は拘留された。

note.ja: ラテン語 custodia（見張り）から。custos（番人）。「保護・拘留・親権」。custodian と同じ。

en: To remove, get rid of or erase, especially written or printed material, or data on a computer or other device.
To remove from a record label's catalog so that it is out of print.
A deletion.
A remainder of a music or video release.

delete.ety:
From Latin dēlētus, past participle of dēlēre (“destroy, blot out, efface”), from dēlēvī, originally perf. tense of dēlinere (“to daub, erase by smudging”), from dē- (“from, away”) + linere (“to smear, wipe”). Original sense first appears c. 1495. In common use for ordering the absence of features of products (such as automobiles) in the 1960s. The computing sense, including the noun form, first appears c. 1977 in Software: Practice & Experience. Not related to deleterious.
Doublet of delible and deleble.

ex.en: Comments not written in English will be deleted.
ex.ja: 英語で書かれていないコメントは削除されます。

ex.en: Please tell me how to delete my account.
ex.ja: アカウントの削除方法を教えてください。

ex.en: "I can't delete the file." "How about now?"
ex.ja: 「ファイル消せない」「これでどう？」

note.ja: ラテン語 delere（消す）から。「削除する」。

en: The act of departing or something that has departed.
A deviation from a plan or procedure.

departure.ety: From Old French deporteure (“departure; figuratively, death”). By surface analysis, depart + -ure.

ex.ja: 彼は出発を延期することを決心した。

ex.en: Her behavior was a departure from the normal.
ex.ja: 彼女の行動は常軌を逸したものだ。

ex.en: I'd like to confirm the hour of departure.
ex.ja: 出発時刻を確認したいのですが。

note.ja: depart（出発する）+ -ure。de + partire（分ける）。「離れること」→「出発」。part と同じ。

en: A person or entity engaged in the creation or improvement of certain classes of products.
A real estate developer; a person or company who prepares a parcel of land for sale, or creates structures on that land.

dig.ety:
From Middle English diggen (“to dig”, 13th c.), an alteration of dīken, from Old English dīcian (“to dig a ditch, mound up earth”), from Proto-West Germanic *dīkōn, which see for cognates. This verb is denominal from Proto-Germanic *dīkaz (“pool, puddle; dyke, ditch”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeygʷ- (“to stab, dig”).
The form with g may have been influenced by Old French *diguer, a variant of dikier, itself from the West Germanic verb above. French forms with g are attested only in the 15th c., thus 200 years later than in English. On the other hand, French has according forms also for the

note.ja: 中英語 diggen から。語源ははっきりしない。「掘る」。

en: A higher than normal body temperature of a person (or, generally, a mammal), usually caused by disease.
Any of various diseases.
To put into a fever; to affect with fever.
To become fevered.

fever.ety: From Middle English fever, fevere, from Old English fefer, fefor (“fever”) and Old French fievre (“fever”), from Latin febris (“a fever”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰegʷʰ- (“to burn”). ex.en: You have a little fever today, don't you?
ex.ja: 今日はちょっと熱があるんだろ？

ex.ja: 少し熱があると思うんだよね。

ex.en: He seems to have a touch of fever.
ex.ja: 彼は少し熱があるようだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 febris（熱）から。「熱」→「熱狂」。February とは別語源。

A liquid (as opposed to a solid or gas).
Of or relating to fluid.
In a state of flux; subject to change.

ex.ja: 水も空気も両方とも流動体である。

ex.ja: 動物は主として液体で構成される体を持つ。

en: The image-making power of the mind; the act of mentally creating or reproducing an object not previously perceived; the ability to create…
Particularly, construction of false images; fantasizing.

imagination.ety: From Middle English ymaginacioun, from Old French imaginacion, ymaginacion, from Latin imāginātiō. Equivalent to imagine + -ation.

ex.en: The exhibition was a product of his imagination.
ex.ja: その展覧会は彼の想像力の産物だった。

ex.en: The music set my imagination to work.
ex.ja: その音楽は私の想像力をかきたてた。

ex.en: I'll leave it up to your imagination.
ex.ja: ご想像にお任せします。

note.ja: imagine（想像する）+ -ation。ラテン語 imago（像）。「心に像を描くこと」。image と同じ。

en: The act or process of making whole or entire.
The process of combining with compatible elements in order to incorporate them.

integration.ety: From French intégration, from Latin integratio. Morphologically integrate + -ion.

ex.ja: 二つの会社の統合は順調に進んだ。

note.ja: integrate（統合する）+ -ion。ラテン語 integer（完全な）。「完全なひとつにすること」→「統合・積分」。integrity と同じ。

en: Steadfast adherence to a strict moral or ethical code.
The state of being wholesome; unimpaired

integrity.ety: Borrowed from Middle French intégrité, from Latin integritās (“soundness, integrity”), from integer. Doublet of entirety.

ex.ja: 彼は正直なのでたくさん友達がいる。

note.ja: ラテン語 integritas（完全さ）から。integer。「完全な状態」→「誠実さ・高潔」。integrate と同じ。

en: An act of interpreting or explaining something unclear; a translation; a version.
A sense given by an interpreter; an exposition or explanation given; meaning.

interpretation.ety: From Middle English interpretacioun, from the Anglo-Norman form of Old French interpretacion, from Latin interpretātiō, noun of action from interpretor (“to explain, expound, interpret, understand, conclude, infer, comprehend”). Morphologically interpret + -ation.

ex.ja: 彼のいったことはいくつかの意味に解釈できます。

ex.ja: 私はあなたの解釈に大いに賛成だ。

ex.ja: その問題には一つの解釈しかない。

note.ja: interpret（解釈する）+ -ation。ラテン語 interpres（仲介者・通訳）。「解釈・通訳」。

Conforming to known principles, or established or accepted rules or standards; valid.
A person born to a legally married couple.
To make legitimate, lawful, or valid; especially, to put in the position or state of a legitimate person before the law, by legal means.

legitimate.ety:
From Middle English legitimat, legytymat, from Medieval Latin lēgitimātus, perfect passive participle of Latin lēgitimō (“to make legal”) (see -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), from Latin lēgitimus (“lawful”), originally "fixed by law, in line with the law," from Latin lēx (“law”). ex.en: I won't divorce you unless you give me a legitimate reason.
ex.ja: ちゃんとした理由をいってくれなければ、君と離婚するつもりはないよ。

ex.ja: 我々は公立図書館を持つことを市民の当然の権利と考えている。

note.ja: ラテン語 legitimus（法にかなった）から。lex（法）。→「合法的な・正当な」。

To allow (someone) to do something; to give permission to.

ex.ja: 我々にはわずかな意見の相違があった。

ex.ja: その社会主義者は女性の通訳を同伴させていた。

en: To file a legal action against someone, generally a non-criminal (civil) action.
To seek by request; to make application; to petition; to entreat; to plead.

ex.ja: スーと私はいつも仲良くやってきた。

en: The condition of being held in a state between two or more forces, which are acting in opposition to each other.
A psychological state of being tense.
To place an object in tension, to pull or place strain on.

ex.ja: その場には緊張感がみなぎっていた。

note.ja: tens（伸ばす）+ ion。ぴんと引き伸ばすこと →「緊張・張力」。

en: The act of conducting or carrying out (business, negotiations, plans).
A deal or business agreement.

transaction.ety: Borrowed from Middle French transaction, from Old French transaccion, from Late Latin transactio. By surface analysis, trans- + action.

ex.en: Do you wish to make any other transaction?
ex.ja: 続けてお取り引きなさいますか。

ex.en: He rejoiced at the successful business transaction.
ex.ja: 彼は商売がうまくいったのを喜んだ。

ex.ja: この取り引きには大金が賭けられている。

note.ja: transact（取引する）+ -ion。trans（越えて）+ agere（行う）。「やり遂げること」→「取引」。

en: A twisting force.
Anything twisted, or the act of twisting.
To turn the ends of something, usually thread, rope etc., in opposite directions, often using force.
To join together by twining one part around another.

ex.ja: もう、なんでそんなひねくれたこと言うの？

ex.en: This mystery has a plot twist that's completely novel.
ex.ja: このミステリーのトリックは、奇想天外だ。

ex.ja: その小道は山中を縫って続いている。

en: Used to express repugnance, disgust, or annoyance.
Used to express inarticulate vocalisations, such as used by a caveman.

ex.en: Ugh, I hate work. I don't wanna go.
ex.ja: 仕事なんか大嫌い。行きたくな〜い。

ex.en: Ugh! I lost my phone again.
ex.ja: げっ！またスマホ落とした。

ex.en: Ugh, the battery just had to die at the worst time.
ex.ja: うわ、最悪なタイミングで電池切れやがった。

note.ja: 嫌悪を表す声。

en: The state of having no job; joblessness.
The phenomenon of joblessness in an economy.

ex.ja: 現在の失業率はどのくらいですか。

ex.ja: 当面の最大問題は失業である。

ex.en: This year unemployment will reach record levels.
ex.ja: 今年は失業者数が記録的になるだろう。

note.ja: un（否定）+ employment（雇用）。「失業」。employ はラテン語 implicare（巻き込む）。

en: Oneness: the state or fact of being one undivided entity.
Agreement; harmony.

unity.ety: From Middle English unite, from Anglo-Norman, Old French unité, from Latin ūnitās, from ūnus (“one”) + noun of state suffix -itās, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *óynos (“one, single”), hence distantly related to one and an. By surface analysis, unite + -y. Displaced native Old English ānnes (literally “oneness”).

ex.en: They live together in unity.
ex.ja: 彼らは仲良く一緒に暮らしている。

ex.en: Unity is our strength!
ex.ja: まとまりは我々の力だ！

ex.en: The figure on the left spoils the unity of the painting.
ex.ja: 左手の人物がその絵の統一性を壊している。

note.ja: ラテン語 unitas（ひとつであること）から。unus（ひとつ）。「団結・統一」。unite、union と同じ。

en: Without use or the possibility to be used.
Unhelpful, not useful; pointless (of an action).

en: Someone who views a spectacle; an onlooker or spectator.
Someone who watches television.

viewer.ety: From Middle English vewer; equivalent to view + -er.

ex.ja: テレビ観戦者はカメラが捕らえるものしか見られない。

ex.ja: テレビは視聴者に娯楽ばかりではなく、知識も与える。

ex.en: The city of Mito was crowded with blossom viewers.
ex.ja: 水戸市は花見客でいっぱいだった。

note.ja: view（見る）+ -er。「視聴者」。view はラテン語 videre（見る）。

en: Someone whose job is to speak for someone's case in a court of law; a counsel.
Anyone who argues the case of another; an intercessor.
To plead in favour of; to defend by argument, before a tribunal or the public; to support, vindicate, or recommend publicly.
To encourage support for something.

advocate.ety:
From Middle English advocat, advoket, from Old French advocat, from Latin advocātus (“an advocate”), from the substantivization of the perfect passive participle of advocāre (“to call for”) (see -ate (noun-forming suffix)), from a calque of Ancient Greek παράκλητος (paráklētos) (whence English paraclete).
Doublet of advoke, avocat, avouch, and avow. The verb derives from the noun on the basis of -ate (verb-forming suffix).

ex.en: He advocated to us that the changes be made.
ex.ja: 彼はその改革を実行すべきだと主張した。

ex.en: He advocates reform of university education.
ex.ja: 彼は大学教育の改革を主張している。

ex.en: She advocated equal rights for women.
ex.ja: 彼女は女性差別撤廃を主張した。

note.ja: ad（〜へ）+ voc（声・呼ぶ）+ ate。〜のために声を上げる →「主張する・擁護者・弁護士」。

A continuous part of the circumference of a circle (circular arc) or of another curve.
To move following a curved path.
To shape into an arc; to hold in the form of an arc.

ex.ja: 虹は空に弓じょうにかかる。

A copy of a file or record, stored separately from the original, that can be used to recover the original if it is damaged or destroyed.

ex.ja: 大丈夫だ。もしXが発生しても、Yでバックアップできる。

A type of beer heavily flavored with hops.

ex.ja: 若者は自分の苦い経験から学ばねばならない。

ex.ja: 戦争中は私たちは多くの辛い思いをした。

ex.ja: 必ずしも苦い薬が行く効くとは限らない。

en: Nimble with hands or body; dexterous; skillful; adept.

ex.ja: 確かに彼は利口な少年だ。

ex.ja: その少年とその少女のどちらも賢い。

ex.ja: 最も利口な生徒でさえもばかげた間違いをすることがある。

Without intervening space; continued.

continuous.ety: From Latin continuus, from contineō (“hold together”). Displaced native Old English singal.

ex.ja: 延々と続く車の列があった。

ex.ja: ここに絶え間ない痛みがあります。

ex.ja: 日本経済は連続６０ヶ月以上の拡大を記録した。

A person who is now in favour of something that they previously opposed or disliked.

ex.ja: その土地は公園に変えられた。

ex.ja: 変換にはかなりの時間がかかる。

ex.ja: 私はその問題に正しく答えることができた。

ex.ja: 郵便の宛名ははっきり正確に。

en: Something or someone which creates or makes something.
The deity that created the world.

ex.ja: 人間は環境によってつくられるものというよりはむしろ環境をつくり出すものなのである。

en: A living being, such as an animal, monster, or alien.
An unidentified, mysterious, and often monstrous animal or being.

ex.en: Were it not for air, no creatures could live.
ex.ja: 空気がもしなかったら、生物は生きることができないでしょう。

ex.en: We are surprised to see how every creature lives.
ex.ja: あらゆる生き物がどのように生きているかを見て私たちは驚く。

ex.en: A strange marine creature was found recently.
ex.ja: 最近変わった海洋生物が発見された。

note.ja: ラテン語 creatura（創造されたもの）から。creare（創造する）。「生き物」。create と同じ。

ex.en: What criteria do you use in deciding who to vote for?
ex.ja: どんな基準で誰に投票するか決めていますか。

note.ja: criterion（基準）の複数形。ギリシャ語 kritērion（判断の手段）、krinein（分ける）。crisis、critic と同じ。

en: A police officer tasked with collecting evidence and information in order to solve a crime; an investigator.
A person employed to find information not otherwise available to the public.
Employed in detecting.
To be or act as or like a detective.
To investigate or find information about (someone or something) as or like a detective.

detective.ety:

ex.en: He would sit for hours reading detective stories.
ex.ja: 彼はよく探偵小説を読んで何時間も座っていたものだ。

ex.en: The man turned out to be a private detective.
ex.ja: その男は私立探偵だとわかった。

ex.en: A detective arrived upon the scene of the crime.
ex.ja: 刑事が犯行現場に到着した。

en: A condition characterised by a significant limitation in a person's physical or intellectual powers or ability.
The state of having such a condition; the state of being disabled.

ex.en: Damn, Jackson! You really have a learning disability!
ex.ja: わあ、ジャクソン！学習障害があるよね！

ex.en: December 3 is the International Day of Persons with Disabilities.

The contents of such a vessel.
To put in a dish or dishes; serve, usually food.
To make concave, or depress in the middle, like a dish.

ex.en: These dishes remind me of my mother's cooking.

en: A quick breaking or cracking sound or the action of producing such a sound.
A sudden break.
To fracture or break apart suddenly.
To give forth or produce a sharp cracking noise; to crack.
The cry used in a game of snap when winning a hand.
"I've got one the same!", "Me too!"
Done, made, performed, etc., quickly and unexpectedly, or without deliberation.

ex.en: This new camera is a snap to use.

en: Of or pertaining to Sweden.
Of or pertaining to the Swedish language.

Swedish.ety: From Swede + -ish. Cognate with Dutch Zweeds, German Schwedisch.

ex.en: I watched a Swedish movie last night.
ex.ja: 私は昨晩スウェーデンの映画を見ました。

ex.ja: 私はフィンランド人なのに、スウェーデン語も話せる。

ex.ja: スウェーデン語を教えてくれないかな？

note.ja: Swede + -ish。古北欧語 Svíar（スウェーデン人）。

en: The act of transforming or the state of being transformed.
A marked change in appearance or character, especially one for the better.

transformation.ety: Inherited from Middle English transformacioun, from Middle French, from Ecclesiastical Latin trānsfōrmātiō. Morphologically transform + -ation.

ex.en: The town has gone through a complete transformation.
ex.ja: その町はすっかり様変わりした。

note.ja: trans（別の状態へ）+ form（形）+ ation。形を別のものに変えること →「変形・変化」。

en: More or most likely to be exposed to the chance of being attacked or harmed, either physically or emotionally.
Open to disclosing one's inner thoughts and feelings, acting in spite of one's instinct to self-preservation.

vulnerable.ety: From Late Latin vulnerābilis (“injurious, wounding”), from Latin vulnerō (“to wound”).

ex.en: Mr Smith is vulnerable to this kind of criticism.
ex.ja: スミス氏はこの種の批判に弱い。

ex.en: One of the areas most vulnerable to sandstorms was Dallam County.
ex.ja: ダラム郡は、砂嵐で最も大きな被害を受けやすい地域の一つでした。

note.ja: ラテン語 vulnerabilis（傷つけうる）から。vulnus（傷）。「傷つきやすい」。

en: Possessing financial wealth; rich.
Abundant in quality or quantity; profuse.
Synonym of rich: the wealthy people of a society or of the world collectively.
A rich person.

wealthy.ety: From Middle English welthy, welþi, equivalent to wealth + -y. Cognate with Middle Dutch weldech, weeldech (“magnificent, luscious, lavish”).

ex.en: The lawyer has a lot of wealthy clients.
ex.ja: その弁護士には金持ちの顧客が多い。

ex.en: Though he is wealthy, he is not happy.
ex.ja: 裕福であるにもかかわらず、彼は幸福ではない。

ex.en: He is a son of a wealthy family.
ex.ja: 彼は裕福な家庭の息子だ。

note.ja: wealth（富）+ -y。「裕福な」。

additionally.ety:

ex.ja: トムもメアリーも個性豊かです。

ex.en: Additionally, the tale starting with "Genji's Story" was also much loved.
ex.ja: また、『源氏物語』をはじめとする物語が愛好されました。

note.ja: additional（追加の）+ -ly。ラテン語 addere ＝ ad + dare（与える）。「さらに」。add と同じ。

Average sensitivity of a security's price to overall securities market prices.
Identifying a molecular position in an organic chemical compound.
Designates the second in an order of precedence.
To preliminarily release computer software for initial testing prior to final release.

ex.ja: アルファ、ベータ、ガンマはギリシャ文字です。

en: A naturally occurring or man-made alloy of copper, usually in combination with tin, but also with one or more other metals.
A reddish-brown colour, the colour of bronze.
Made of bronze metal.
Having a reddish-brown colour.
To plate with bronze.

ex.en: The sun has bronzed her skin.
ex.ja: 彼女は日焼けしてブロンズ色になった。

ex.en: The bronze statue looks quite nice from a distance.
ex.ja: その銅像を遠くから見るとかなり素敵に見えます。

ex.en: They set up a bronze statue of the hero.
ex.ja: 彼らはその英雄の銅像を建てた。

note.ja: イタリア語 bronzo から。ペルシャ語 birinj（銅）とされる。「青銅」→ 3位の「銅メダル」。

en: An insect of the order Hemiptera (the “true bugs”).
Any motile small terrestrial invertebrate, especially one that is seen as a pest.
To annoy.
To act suspiciously or irrationally, especially in a way that annoys others.

bug.ety:
First attested in this form around 1620 (referring to a “bedbug”), from earlier bugge (“beetle”), from Middle English bugge (“scarecrow, hobgoblin”) which is traced alternatively to:
* a Celtic root found in Scots bogill (“goblin, bugbear”) and obsolete Welsh bwg (“ghost, hobgoblin”); compare Welsh bwgwl (“threat, fear”) and Middle Irish bocanách (“supernatural being”).
* Proto-Germanic *bugja- (“swollen up, thick”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰew-, *bu- (“to swell”); compare Norwegian bugge (“big man”), dialectal Low German Bögge (“goblin, snot”).
* or to a word related to buck and originally

ex.en: Stop bugging me with your annoying questions!
ex.ja: くどいよ君の質問は、もううるさい。

ex.en: The birds ate the bugs taking turns.
ex.ja: 鳥が虫を交替で食べました。

ex.en: I think I caught a bug over the weekend.
ex.ja: 週末に風邪をひいたみたいなんだ。

note.ja: 中英語 bugge（お化け）からとされる。「虫」→ 機械の不具合「バグ」→ 盗聴器。

en: A large, naturally-occurring cavity formed underground or in the face of a cliff or a hillside.
A hole, depression, or gap in earth or rock, whether natural or man-made.
To surrender.
To collapse.
look out!; beware!

cave.ety: From Middle English cave, borrowed from Old French cave, from Latin cava (“cavity”), from cavus (“hollow”). Cognate with Tocharian B kor (“throat”), Albanian cup (“odd, uneven”), Ancient Greek κύαρ (kúar, “eye of needle, earhole”), Old Armenian սոր (sor, “hole”), Sanskrit शून्य (śūnya, “empty, barren, zero”). Displaced native Old English sċræf. More at cavum, cavus and cage.

ex.en: This is what I found in the cave.
ex.ja: これは私が洞窟の中で見つけたものです。

ex.en: Was the cave found by the boys?
ex.ja: その洞穴はその少年たちによって発見されたのですか。

ex.en: A monster was believed to live in the cave.
ex.ja: その洞窟には怪物が住んでいると信じられていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 cavus（中空の）から。「洞窟」。cavity（虫歯の穴）と同じ。

en: An act of deception, fraud, trickery, imposture, imposition or infidelity.
The arrangement of people or items in a film so as to give the (false) impression that shots are taken from different angles in the same …
Unsporting or underhand.
Unfaithful or adulterous.

ex.en: If you do that, you will be cheating.
ex.ja: そんなことをすれば、人をだますことになる。

ex.ja: 先に駆け出すなんてずるいぞ。

ex.en: You shouldn't let him get away with cheating.
ex.ja: 彼が人をだますようなことをするのをほっといてはいけない。

note.ja: cheat（だます）+ -ing。cheat は escheat（没収）の短縮。「不正に取り上げる」→「だます」。

Prolonged or slow to heal.
A condition of extended duration, either continuous or marked by frequent recurrence. Sometimes implies a condition which worsens with ea…
A person who is chronic, such as a criminal reoffender or a person with chronic disease.

ex.ja: ここに慢性の痛みがあります。

ex.en: There is a chronic oversupply of rice in Japan.
ex.ja: 日本では米が恒常的に供給過剰である。

ex.ja: 彼女は慢性疾患で苦しんでいる。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 chronos（時）から。時間が長く続く →「慢性の・常習的な」。chronology（年代順の記録）も同じ。

en: To impart or transmit (information or knowledge) to someone; to make known, to tell.
To impart or transmit (an intangible quantity, substance); to give a share of.

communicate.ety: Adapted borrowing of Latin commūnicāt- (past participial stem of commūnicō (“share, impart; make common”)) + -ate (verb-forming suffix), from commūnis (“common”) + -icō. Compare French communiquer and its older (and now obsolete) English cognate from Middle French, communique.

ex.en: They communicate with each other often by mail.
ex.ja: しばしば手紙で連絡しあっている。

ex.en: This ability to communicate helps us a lot.
ex.ja: この意志を伝えることができる能力は私たちにとても役立っている。

ex.en: We need to communicate with each other.
ex.ja: 我々は互いにコミュニケーションをとる必要がある。

note.ja: com（共に）+ mun（務め）+ ic + ate。共有のものにする →「伝える・意思疎通する」。

en: To find guilty, as a result of legal proceedings, or (informal) in a moral sense.
To convince, persuade; to cause (someone) to believe in (something).
A person convicted of a crime by a judicial body.
A person deported to a penal colony.

convict.ety: From Middle English convicten, from Anglo-Norman convicter, from Latin convictus, the past participle of convincō (“to convict”). Doublet of convince. Displaced native Old English forwyrċan (“to convict, condemn”).

ex.en: No one has been convicted of the crime yet.
ex.ja: まだ誰もその犯罪で有罪判決を受けていない。

ex.en: There wasn't enough evidence to convict him of the crime.
ex.ja: 彼を有罪とするのに十分な証拠がなかった。

ex.en: The convict was pardoned after serving his sentence.
ex.ja: その囚人は刑期に服した後赦免された。

note.ja: con（完全に）+ vict（打ち勝つ）。法廷で完全に打ち負かす →「有罪を宣告する・囚人」。

The process of, or an instance of, identification of the nature and cause of something (of any nature).

ex.ja: 一週間後に治らなければ、医師の診断が必要です。

To order to leave.

ex.ja: まず第一に私たちはその料理人を解雇しなければならない。

ex.ja: あなたを解雇する十分な理由があります。

en: To recognize someone or something as different from others based on its characteristics.
To see someone or something clearly or distinctly.

distinguish.ety: From Middle English distingwen, from Old French distinguer, from Latin distinguere (“to separate, divide, distinguish, set off, adorn, literally mark off”), from di-, dis- (“apart”) + stinguere, related to English stink. Compare extinguish.

ex.en: We cannot distinguish her from her younger sister.
ex.ja: 我々は彼女と彼女の妹を区別できない。

ex.en: The original and the copy are easily distinguished.
ex.ja: 原稿とコピーは容易に見分けが付く。

ex.en: Sometimes reality and fantasy are hard to distinguish.
ex.ja: 時には現実と幻想を区別するのは難しい。

en: A measured portion of medicine taken at any one time.
The quantity of an agent (not always active), substance, or radiation administered or experienced at any one time.
To administer a dose (of medicine) to.
To prescribe a dose.

dose.ety: Borrowed from Middle French dose, from Late Latin dosis, from Ancient Greek δόσις (dósis, “a portion prescribed”, literally “a giving”), used by Galen and other Greek physicians to mean an amount of medicine, from δίδωμι (dídōmi, “to give”). ex.en: It's time you had a dose of your medicine.
ex.ja: もう薬を一服飲む時間ですよ。

ex.ja: ６時おきに彼に薬を一服飲ませてください。

ex.ja: １日に３度１錠ずつ服用してください。

The person or thing in the eighth position.
One of eight equal parts of a whole.
To divide by eight.

ex.en: I think eighth grade was the most fun.
ex.ja: 中2のときが一番楽しかった気がする。

ex.ja: 「８月」は１年の中で８回目の月にあたります。

ex.ja: 私の家は８階にあります。

en: The soft tissue of the body, especially muscle and fat.
The skin of a human or animal.
To reward (a hound, bird of prey etc.) with flesh of the animal killed, to excite it for further hunting; to train (an animal) to have an…
To bury (something, especially a weapon) in flesh.

ex.en: She lost one of her flesh and blood.
ex.ja: 彼女は肉親の一人を失った。

ex.en: The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.
ex.ja: 心熱けれど肉体は弱し。

ex.en: I have seen him on TV but not in the flesh.
ex.ja: テレビで見たことはあるが直接本人に会ったことはない。

note.ja: 古英語 flǣsc から。「肉」→ 精神に対する「肉体」。

en: A maneuver which rotates an object end over end.
A complete change of direction, decision, movement etc.
To throw so as to turn over.
To put into a quick revolving motion through a snap of the thumb and index finger.
Used to express annoyance, especially when the speaker has made an error.
Having the quality of playfulness, or lacking seriousness of purpose.
Sarcastic.

ex.ja: 授業中によくパラパラ漫画作ってたなぁ。

ex.en: You see, I often made flip-books during lessons.
ex.ja: 授業中によくパラパラ漫画作ってたなぁ。

note.ja: 16世紀からの語。擬音的な語とされる。「はじく」→「ひっくり返す」。flop と同系。

Resembling or characteristic of a fort.

ex.ja: トムは普通１０時４０分に床に就きます。

ex.ja: スミス氏が４０年前にこの学校を創立した。

ex.ja: あの婦人はせいぜい４０歳だ。

generous.ety: From Middle French genereux, and its source, Latin generōsus (“of noble birth”), from genus (“race, stock”).

ex.ja: 君は彼の寛大な性格に付け込むべきではない。

ex.en: Bacteria are invisible to the naked eye.
ex.ja: バクテリアは肉眼では見えない。

ex.en: Bacteria will not breed in alcohol.
ex.ja: バクテリアはアルコールの中では繁殖しない。

ex.en: Bacteria are just tiny harmless cells.
ex.ja: 細菌はただの小さい細胞で、無害です。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 baktērion（小さな杖）から。棒状の細菌が最初に見つかったことから。単数形は bacterium。

en: Next to; at the side of.
Not relevant to.
Otherwise; else; in addition; besides.

beside.ety: From Middle English beside, besiden, bisyde (also besides > besides), from Old English be sīdan, bī sīdan (“by the side (of), on the side (of)”). Compare Saterland Frisian biesiede (“aside”), German Low German bisied (“aside”), German beiseite (“aside, to one side”). Compare also Dutch terzijde (“aside”). By surface analysis, be- + side.

ex.en: The cat has just passed by beside me.
ex.ja: ねこが私のそばを丁度今横切った。

ex.en: Who is the pretty girl sitting beside Jack?
ex.ja: ジャックのそばに座っているきれいな女の子は誰だ。

ex.en: The successful candidates were beside themselves with joy.
ex.ja: 合格者たちは喜びのあまり我を忘れた。

note.ja: by + side（そば）。「〜のそばに」→「〜と比べると」。besides（〜のほかに）と区別。

en: The (typically sharp-edged) part of a knife, sword, razor, or other tool with which it cuts.
A sword or knife.
To skate on rollerblades.
To furnish with a blade.

blade.ety:

Cognate with West Frisian bled, German Blatt, Danish, Dutch, Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, and Swedish blad, Faroese and Icelandic blað, Irish bláth (“flower”), Welsh blodyn (“flower”), Tocharian A pält, Tocharian B pil

ex.en: I cut my finger with a razor blade.
ex.ja: かみそりの刃で指を切りました。

ex.en: The knife has a keen blade.
ex.ja: そのナイフはよく切れる。

note.ja: 古英語 blæd（葉）から。葉の形 →「刃」→ プロペラの「羽根」。草の葉は今も blade of grass。

en: Size, specifically, volume.
Any huge body or structure.
Being large in size, mass, or volume (of goods, etc.).
Total.
To appear or seem to be, as to bulk or extent.
To grow in size; to swell or expand.

bulk.ety:
From Middle English bulk, bolke (“a heap, cargo, hold; heap; bulge”), borrowed from Old Norse búlki (“the freight or the cargo of a ship”), from Proto-Germanic *bulkô (“beam, pile, heap”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰelǵ- (“beam, pile, prop”). Compare Icelandic búlkast (“to be bulky”), Swedish dialectal bulk (“a bunch”), Danish bulk (“bump, knob”).
Conflated with Middle English bouk (“belly, trunk”).

ex.en: Great bulk does not always mean great weight.
ex.ja: 体積が大きいからといって常に重量も重いとは限らない。

ex.en: You can get anything less expensive in bulk.
ex.ja: 物はすべて一括して買うとやすい。

ex.en: He finished the bulk of his work before dinner.
ex.ja: 彼は夕食前に仕事の大部分を終えた。

note.ja: 古北欧語 búlki（積み荷）から。「かさ」→「大部分・大量」。

en: Freight carried by a ship, aircraft, or motor vehicle.
Western material goods.
To load with freight.

cargo.ety: Borrowed from Spanish cargo (“load, burden”), from cargar (“to load”), from Late Latin carricō. Doublet of charge and carga. Displaced native Old English fearm.

ex.en: It's a cargo ship.
ex.ja: 貨物船だよ。

ex.en: The ship discharged its cargo in Panama.
ex.ja: 船はパナマで荷を降ろした。

ex.en: A cargo vessel, bound for Athens, sank in the Mediterranean without a trace.
ex.ja: アテネへ向かう一隻の貨物船が何の痕跡も残さずに地中海で沈没した。

note.ja: スペイン語 cargo（積み荷）から。cargar（積む）、ラテン語 carricare。car、charge と同じ語源。

en: An official count or enumeration of members of a population (not necessarily human), usually residents or citizens in a particular region…
The people being treated in a healthcare facility, clinic or program.
To conduct a census on.
To collect a census.

census.ety: Borrowed from Latin cēnsus, from cēnseō. See censor.

ex.en: In Japan, a census is taken every five years.
ex.ja: 日本では５年に一度国勢調査が行われます。

ex.en: In Japan, a census is conducted every five years.
ex.ja: 日本では５年に一度国勢調査が行われます。

ex.en: In the United States, there is a census every ten years.
ex.ja: 合衆国では１０年に一度国勢調査が行われる。

note.ja: ラテン語 census（財産の査定）から。censere（評価する）。古代ローマの人口・財産調査 →「国勢調査」。censor と同じ。

en: Relating to the coast; on or near the coast; longshore.

ex.ja: 数年後、ヨーロッパ人たちは沿岸の植民地に住み着いた。

ex.en: The coastal ecosystem of British Columbia is rapidly declining.
ex.ja: ブリティッシュコロンビアの沿岸生態系の劣化が急速に進行している。

note.ja: coast（海岸）+ -al。「沿岸の」。

en: A series of comments or annotations; especially, a book of explanations or expositions on the whole or a part of some other work.
A brief account of transactions or events written hastily, as if for a memorandum.

commentary.ety: From Middle French commentaire, from Latin commentārius, commentārium (“notebook”), compare French commentaire. See comment.

ex.en: We listened to the live commentary on the radio.
ex.ja: 私たちはラジオで実況を聞いた。

note.ja: com（完全に）+ ment（心）+ ary。心に浮かんだことを書き留めたもの →「解説・論評・実況」。comment（論評）。

en: A lack of clarity or order.
The state of being confused; misunderstanding.

confusion.ety:
From Middle English confusioun, from Old French confusion, from Latin confusio, confusionem.
Morphologically confuse + -ion.

ex.en: In a sense, I can understand his confusion.
ex.ja: ある程度は彼の困惑も理解できる。

ex.en: She took advantage of his confusion to escape.
ex.ja: 彼がうろたえてるすきにすかさず彼女は逃げた。

ex.en: There has been a little confusion of names.
ex.ja: 名前の混同が少しあった。

note.ja: confuse（混乱させる）+ -ion。con + fundere（注ぐ）。「一緒に注ぎ混ぜる」→「混乱」。fusion と同じ fus。

ex.ja: 議会の公聴会は６時間続いた。

note.ja: congress（議会）+ -ional。ラテン語 congressus（集まり）、com + gradi（歩む）。「議会の」。

en: Any cereal plant (or its grain) that is the main crop or staple of a country or region.
Maize, a grain crop of the species Zea mays.
To granulate; to form (a substance) into grains.
To preserve using coarse salt, e.g. corned beef.

ex.en: I have a corn on my right foot.
ex.ja: 右脚にうおのめができています。

ex.en: When is the best time to plant corn?
ex.ja: トウモロコシを植えるのに最適な時期はいつですか？

ex.en: I have had a corn removed from my foot.
ex.ja: 足の魚の目を取ってもらいました。

note.ja: 古英語 corn（穀粒）から。grain と同じ祖先。アメリカでは「トウモロコシ」、イギリスでは「穀物」。足の「うおのめ」はラテン語 cornu（角）からで別語。

A drug dealer, one who peddles illicit drugs.

ex.ja: 彼は魚屋です。

ex.en: The winner received a new car from a local car dealer.
ex.ja: 優勝者には、地元のカーディーラーから新車が贈呈されました。

note.ja: deal（取引する・配る）+ -er。「販売業者」→ トランプの「配り手」。

en: An accreditation awarded to higher educational institutions in India.

ex.en: He deemed it wise to accept the offer.
ex.ja: 彼は申し出を受諾することが賢明だと考えた。

ex.en: The boy deemed that he cheated in the examination.
ex.ja: その男の子はその試験でカンニングしたことを拒否した。

ex.en: Having said 'domestic wine', anything bottled domestically is deemed to be domestic wine.
ex.ja: しかし、国産ワインといっても、国内で瓶詰めされたものは全て国産ワインとなります。

note.ja: deem（〜と見なす）+ -ed。古英語 dēman（判断する）。doom（運命・判決）と同じ語源。

en: That to which any person or thing is destined; a predetermined or inevitable eventual state; a condition predestined by the Divine or by …
One's eventual fate (not necessarily inevitable or predestined).

destiny.ety: From Middle English destine et al., from Old French destinee, from Latin dēstinō (English destine). Displaced Old English wyrd.

ex.en: You are the master of your own destiny.
ex.ja: 君は君自身の運命の主でもあります。

ex.en: No one can be more wise than destiny.
ex.ja: 何人も運命より賢明ではあり得ない。

ex.en: People should be the masters of their own destinies.
ex.ja: 人は皆自己の運命の支配者になるべきだ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 destinee から。ラテン語 destinare（定める）。「定められたもの」→「運命」。destination と同じ。

Emotionally unresponsive or unwilling to express genuine feelings.

ex.ja: 私たちは互いに何マイルも離れたところで住んでいる。

ex.en: The sun is so distant from the earth.
ex.ja: 太陽は地球からとても遠い。

ex.en: The moon is distant from the earth.
ex.ja: 月は地球から遠い。

note.ja: di（離れて）+ stan（立つ）+ t。離れて立っている →「遠い・よそよそしい」。distance（距離）。

en: To come into view.
To come out of a situation, object, or a liquid.

emerge.ety: First attested in the late 16th century. Borrowed from Middle French emerger, from Latin ēmergō (“to rise up or out”), from ē- (a variant of ex- (“out, forth”)) + mergō (“to dip, to sink”)

ex.en: Five minutes later she emerged from the kitchen.
ex.ja: 五分後、彼女は台所から現れた。

ex.en: A few important facts emerged after the investigation.
ex.ja: 調査の後で２、３の重要な事実が明るみにでた。

ex.en: The moon emerged from behind the cloud.
ex.ja: 月が雲の後ろから現れた。

note.ja: e（外へ）+ merg（浸る）+ e。水中から外へ出る →「現れる・浮かび上がる」。

en: Special weight or forcefulness given to something considered important.
Special attention or prominence given to something.

emphasis.ety: From Latin emphasis, from Ancient Greek ἔμφασις (émphasis, “significance”), from ἐμφαίνω (emphaínō, “to present; to indicate”), from ἐν- (en-, “in”) + φαίνω (phaínō, “to show”).

ex.en: He put too much emphasis on the matter.
ex.ja: 彼はその問題を強調しすぎた。

ex.en: He placed emphasis on the importance of education.
ex.ja: 彼は教育の重要性を強調した。

ex.en: We should not place too much emphasis on money.
ex.ja: 金銭を重視しすぎてはいけない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 emphasis（表れ）から。en（中に）+ phainein（見せる）。「はっきり見せること」→「強調」。phenomenon と同じ。

en: Morality.
The standards that govern the conduct of a person, especially a member of a profession.

ethics.ety: From Middle English etik, from Middle French ethique, from Late Latin ethica, from Ancient Greek ἠθική (ēthikḗ), from ἠθικός (ēthikós, “of or for morals, moral, expressing character”), from ἦθος (êthos, “character, moral nature”).

ex.en: Ethics means the rules of conduct.
ex.ja: 倫理学というのは、行動の規範を意味する。

ex.en: The paper discusses the problem in terms of ethics.
ex.ja: この論文は倫理学の面からその問題を論じている。

ex.en: A great many people were opposed to gene therapy in terms of ethics.
ex.ja: たくさんの人々が倫理の面から遺伝子治療に反対した。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 ēthikos（習慣の・性格の）から。ēthos（習慣）。「倫理（学）」。ethos と同じ。

en: The state of being excited (emotionally aroused).
Something that excites.

excitement.ety: From Middle English excitement, from Old French excitement, equivalent to excite + -ment.

ex.en: There was an air of excitement at the meeting.
ex.ja: 会議は熱気に包まれていた。

ex.en: We watched the baseball game with excitement.
ex.ja: 私たちは手に汗を握って野球の試合を見た。

ex.en: The news of his arrival added to our excitement.
ex.ja: 彼の到着の知らせで我々の興奮は高まった。

note.ja: excite（興奮させる）+ -ment。「興奮」。

en: The process of exploring.
The process of penetrating, or ranging over for purposes of (especially geographical) discovery.

exploration.ety: From Middle French exploration, from Latin exploratio. Morphologically explore + -ation.

ex.en: He likes to go on explorations to Africa.
ex.ja: 彼はアフリカへ探検旅行に行くのが好きだ。

ex.en: Japan will soon start to engage in the exploration of the universe.
ex.ja: 日本はすぐに宇宙開発に乗り出すだろう。

ex.en: Voyages of exploration were the earliest in the history of studying the ocean.
ex.ja: 海洋研究の歴史の先駆けとなったのは、探検のための航海だった。

note.ja: explore（探検する）+ -ation。「探検・調査」。

ex.en: Our teacher has a wonderful sense of humor.
ex.ja: 私たちの先生は実にユーモアのセンスがある。

ex.en: I am in no humor for reading now.
ex.ja: 私は今、本を読む気がしない。

ex.en: I am not a woman with strange humors.
ex.ja: 私は人と変わった気質をもった女ではありません。

note.ja: ラテン語 umor（体液）から。体液のバランスが気質を決めると考えられた →「気分」→「ユーモア」。humid と同じ。

en: A sight or view of the interior of anything; a deep inspection or view; introspection; frequently used with into.
Power of acute observation and deduction.

insight.ety: From Middle English insight, insiht (“insight, mental vision, intelligence, understanding”), equivalent to in- + sight. Perhaps continuing Old English insiht (“narrative, argument, account”), from Proto-Germanic *insahtiz (“account, narrative, argument”). Compare West Frisian ynsjoch (“insight”), Dutch inzicht (“insight, awareness, view, opinion”), German Low German Insicht (“insight”), German Einsicht (“insight, knowledge, perception, understanding”), Danish indsigt (“insight”), Swedish insikt (“insight”), Icelandic innsýn (“insight”).

ex.en: He gave them the benefit of his insight.
ex.ja: 彼は自分の洞察力という利益を彼らに与えてやった。

ex.en: She gave them the benefit of her insight.
ex.ja: 彼女は自分の洞察力という利益を彼らに与えてやった。

ex.en: He has a deep insight into human psychology.
ex.ja: 彼は人間の心理に対する深い洞察力を持っている。

note.ja: in（中を）+ sight（見ること）。「中を見通す力」→「洞察」。

en: A bundle of neurons with their connective tissue sheaths, blood vessels and lymphatics.
A vein in a leaf; a grain in wood.
To give courage.
To give strength; to supply energy or vigour.

nerve.ety:
Recorded since circa 1374 as Middle English nerve, from Medieval Latin nervus (“nerve”), from Latin nervus (“sinew”). Doublet of neuron and sinew.
Verb sense 4 (“to get on (someone’s) nerves”) is chiefly a semantic loan from German nerven.

ex.en: His nerve failed him at the last moment.
ex.ja: いよいよという時になって彼は怖じ気付いた。

ex.en: A man like that gets on my nerves.
ex.ja: ああいう人は神経にさわる。

ex.en: My husband damaged a nerve in his neck.
ex.ja: 私の夫は首の神経を痛めた。

note.ja: ラテン語 nervus（腱・筋）から。「神経」→「度胸」→（nerves）神経の高ぶり =「緊張」。nervous と同じ。

en: A very unpleasant or frightening dream.
Any bad, miserable, difficult or terrifying situation or experience that arouses anxiety, terror, agony or great displeasure.
To experience a nightmare.
To imagine (someone or something) as in a nightmare.

ex.en: I had a nightmare last night.
ex.ja: 昨夜は悪い夢を見た。

ex.en: It's just like a nightmare.
ex.ja: まるで悪夢を見ているようです。

ex.en: It was only a nightmare.
ex.ja: ただの悪夢だった。

note.ja: night（夜）+ mare（眠る人を苦しめる悪霊）。「夜の悪霊」→「悪夢」。mare（雌馬）とは別語。

en: During or throughout the night, especially during the evening or night just past.
In a very short (but unspecified) amount of time.
Occurring between dusk and dawn.
Complete before the next morning.
To stay overnight; to spend the night.
To send something for delivery the next day.
An item delivered or completed overnight.
An overnight stay, especially in a hotel or other lodging facility.

overnight.ety: Inherited from Middle English overnyght, from Old English ofer niht (“through the night, overnight”), equivalent to over + night. ex.en: The stock has gone down overnight.
ex.ja: 株式は一晩のうちに下がった。

ex.en: I'd like to stay here overnight.
ex.ja: 宿泊したいのですが。

ex.en: The clothes soaked in water overnight were heavy.
ex.ja: 一晩水につかっていた着物はずっしり重たかった。

note.ja: over（越えて）+ night。「一夜を越えて」→「一晩中・一夜にして」。

Any of various other, non-pastry dishes that maintain the general concept of a shell with a filling.
To hit in the face with a pie, either for comic effect or as a means of protest (see also pieing).
To go around (a corner) in a guarded manner.

pie.ety:
From Middle English pye, pie, pey (“baked dish, filled pastry”), possibly attested earlier (c. 1199) in the surname Piehus (“pie-house?”). Further origin uncertain.
Relation to Middle English pie, pye (“magpie”) has been suggested due to correspondences between other similar foods and the names of birds (compare haggis (“Scottish dish”) and haggess (“magpie”); and chewet (“meat pie”) and chewet (“chough, jackdaw”); however, the baked dish may instead be named after a creator with the surname Pie, a common name at the time.
The surname is ultimately derived from the bird above, and thus from Ol

en: Inclination towards something.
The diagonal line between warp and weft in a woven fabric.
To place bias upon; to influence.
To give a bias to.
Inclined to one side; swelled on one side.
Cut slanting or diagonally, as cloth.
In a slanting manner; crosswise; obliquely; diagonally.

bias.ety:
c. 1520 in the sense "oblique line". As a technical term in the game of bowls c. 1560, whence the figurative use (c. 1570).
From Middle French biais, adverbially ("sideways, askance, against the grain") c. 1250, as a noun ("oblique angle, slant") from the late 16th century.
The French word is likely from Old Occitan biais, itself of obscure origin, most likely from Vulgar Latin *biaxius (“with two axes”).

ex.en: You have to judge the case without bias.
ex.ja: 君はその問題を公正に判断しなければならない。

ex.en: People tend to look at others with bias.
ex.ja: 人々は他人を偏見で見がちだ。

ex.en: I suspect that Tom and Mary are biased.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーは先入観にとらわれているんじゃないかな。

note.ja: フランス語 biais（斜め）から。「斜め」→「偏り・偏見」。布の「バイアス（斜め）」と同じ。

en: A fabric used as a complete floor covering.

To lay carpet, or to have carpet installed, in an area.
To substantially cover something, as a carpet does; to blanket something.

ex.ja: その床には厚いじゅうたんが敷いてある。

ex.en: I'm looking for something to clean the carpet with.
ex.ja: じゅうたんをきれいにする道具を探しているのです。

note.ja: 古イタリア語 carpita（毛布）から。ラテン語 carpere（むしる）。むしった羊毛で作ったもの。
